memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And the Lord God said, "The man has now become like one of us, knowing good and evil. He must not be allowed to reach out his hand and take also from the tree of life and eat, and live forever." So the Lord God banished him from the Garden of Eden to work the ground from which he had been taken. After he drove the man out, he placed on the east side of the Garden of Eden cherubim and a flaming sword flashing back and forth to guard the way to the tree of life. — Gen 3:22–24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
So the chapter closes with Adam and Eve sent out of the garden, and the way back guarded by cherubim and a flaming sword. At first this seems like pure judgment — and it is serious. But look more closely, and even here mercy is woven through.

Why does God bar the way to the tree of life? So that fallen humanity would not eat and "live forever" in a state of sin. Imagine the horror of living endlessly, never able to die, yet trapped forever in brokenness and shame. In love, God does not permit it. The closing of Eden is not only a punishment; it is a mercy that keeps the door open for a better rescue than staying in the garden ever could have been.

For the way back to life is not finally shut — it is guarded, held in reserve, until God Himself opens it again. And He would. The flaming sword that fell on sin would one day fall on Christ in our place, so that the way to the tree of life could be flung wide open.

Dear friend, if you have ever felt shut out — from a place, a season, a life you longed for — take heart. God's closed doors are never the end of His story. The One who guarded the tree of life in Eden now welcomes His people to it freely, for in the New Jerusalem the tree of life stands open to all who are His (Rev 22:2,14). What was lost in the first garden is more than restored in the last.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have you experienced a "closed door" that felt like loss but may have been mercy?
2. How does it change things to see even God's judgments carrying His grace?
3. How does the promise of the tree of life in Revelation fill you with hope?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that even when You closed the garden, You were opening the way to something greater in Christ. Help me to trust that Your closed doors are never without mercy. Thank You that in Jesus the way to the tree of life stands open to me forever. Amen.
